diagnosis.root_cause: In patient/api_gateway/app/main.py, chat_stream creates the gateway->retrieval httpx client with timeout=0.05 (line 511), with the comment 'Retrieval answers in ~30 ms; fail fast'. The doctor's metrics put retrieval's normal /retrieve p95 at about 0.054 s, rising to about 0.1 s under the current load. So a large share of healthy retrieval calls exceed 50 ms and raise httpx.ReadTimeout (and ConnectTimeout when connecting takes more than 50 ms). The error surfaces at the telemetry transport wrapper's handle_async_request frame (patient/common/telemetry.py:194, per the stack trace); the timeout value itself comes from main.py. The chat then gets no document context, which leads to refusals and errors. According to the doctor's report and a prior bug record, the 0.05 value replaced 30.0 and was shipped once before (cf515c9) and reverted (1c5b681); I did not check the git history myself. The smallest fix is to restore timeout=30.0 on the retrieval client in chat_stream. That matches the sibling /api/retrieval/search client at line 360 and the >=20 s requirement in faults/acceptance/test_f6_tight_timeout.py. The LLM stream client in the same function (line 575, timeout=120.0) already complies. Higher traffic is a contributing factor only, not the cause.
evidence: patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:510-511: comment 'Retrieval answers in ~30 ms; fail fast' followed by `async with telemetry.async_client("gateway", timeout=0.05) as client:`

patch.rationale:
Root cause: commit 3bf46d7 set the gateway->retrieval httpx client in chat_stream (patient/api_gateway/app/main.py, around line 511) to timeout=0.05. Retrieval's normal p95 is about 0.054 s and reaches about 0.1 s under the current load, so many healthy calls exceed the limit. They raise httpx.ReadTimeout or ConnectTimeout, which surface in the telemetry transport wrapper at patient/common/telemetry.py:194, and the chat is left with no document context.

Fix: restore timeout=30.0 on that client. This is the value it had before, as the injected-fault text in faults/catalog.py and the earlier revert 1c5b681 both show. It also matches the sibling /retrieve call in the debug_retrieval endpoint and satisfies faults/acceptance/test_f6_tight_timeout.py, which requires every async_client timeout in chat_stream to be >= 20. A 30 s limit still stops a stuck call from hanging forever.

The find string has no leading indentation because line 511 was not in the provided excerpt. It is the exact call quoted in the diagnosis and the doctor's diff, and it should occur only once in the file. All other async_client calls use different timeouts: 3.0, 300.0, 30.0 and 120.0.

The stale comment above this line ('Retrieval answers in ~30 ms; fail fast') is left alone so the change stays minimal and the find text stays exact. A follow-up should correct it so the 0.05 value does not get reintroduced a third time.
